summary: Turns the search page into a client component. It reads q from the URL, fetches matching products and renders them in a list.

findings.title: URL query injected as raw HTML
findings.problem: The heading puts the q URL parameter into dangerouslySetInnerHTML without escaping. React therefore renders attacker-supplied markup as HTML.
findings.consequence: An attacker can send a crafted search link that runs script in the victim's session. That script can steal data or act as the victim.
findings.fix: Render the query as a normal text child so React escapes it.

findings.title: Effect without dependencies refetches forever
findings.problem: The effect has no dependency array, so it runs after every render. Each response calls setResults with a new array, which triggers another render and another fetch.
findings.consequence: The page sends search requests in an endless loop. This loads the catalog API and wastes the user's bandwidth.
findings.fix: Give the effect a dependency array containing query.

findings.title: Hooks called after a conditional return
findings.problem: The early return for an empty query runs before useState and useEffect. The component therefore calls a different number of hooks depending on q.
findings.consequence: React throws a hooks-order error when q is added or cleared during client navigation. The page then crashes.
findings.fix: Call useState and useEffect before the early return. Inside the effect, skip the fetch when query is empty.

findings.title: Search form removed with no replacement
findings.problem: The change deletes the search form. Without q, the page now only says to type a search term and gives no input.
findings.consequence: Users who open /search directly have no way to enter a query.
findings.fix: Keep the form with the q input on the page, at least when no query is present.

findings.title: Search failure rejection is never handled
findings.problem: searchProducts throws when the response is not ok, but the effect chains no catch. The rejected promise floats unhandled.
findings.consequence: A failed search shows the user an empty list with no error message. The browser also logs an unhandled rejection.
findings.fix: Add a catch that records an error state and renders a failure message.

findings.title: New search behaviour has no covering test
findings.problem: SearchPage now fetches and renders results from the URL query. No test in the change covers this behaviour.
findings.consequence: Regressions in the fetch, empty-query or rendering paths can ship unnoticed.
findings.fix: Add a component test that mocks searchProducts and checks the empty-query and results cases.

dropped.reason: The list items are stateless text elements, and each fetch replaces the whole list. A missing key here only causes a dev warning.
